### Below you will find the code associated with "Marine Protected Areas improve age structure of tropical Pacific tunas" by Jaskiel et al.

### All code and data can be found on GitHub (https://github.com/jaskielj/MPA-Effects-on-Tropical-Tuna-Size-Structure) and Zenodo ()

### Set Directory, Install/library packages, & bring in data
```{r}
setwd("/Users/Jacob/Documents/MPA Effects on Tuna Size Structure")
getwd()

library(tidyverse)
library(ggridges)

length <- read_rds("wcpfc_length_data.rds")
catch_purse_seine <- read_rds("allrfmo_month_1deg_purseseine.rds")
catch_longline <- read_rds("allrfmo_month_5deg_longline_flag.rds")
```


### Adding some scripts from Lynham and Villasenor-Derbez (2024) to use a spatial grid rather than what I've been using, which has been coarse latitude and longitude-based analyses that didn't allow for precise calculation of changes in tuna length near (<100 nm) and far (100-200 nm) from each MPA
### From https://github.com/jcvdav/LSMPA_spillover
```{r}
## SET UP ######################################################################
#install.packages("pacman")
library(pacman)

# Load packages ----------------------------------------------------------------
pacman::p_load(
  magrittr,
  here,
  terra,
  sf,
  units,
  tidyverse
)

# Source custom functions ------------------------------------------------------
### downloaded 00_set_up.R from https://github.com/jcvdav/LSMPA_spillover/blob/main
### This document has necessary custom functions and color pallettes, amongst other things
source("00_set_up.R") 

# Define functions -------------------------------------------------------------
# This function assigns a "near" or "far" category to each point, depending on
# the value of x and the distance to an MPA
assign_near_far <- function(dist, x){
  case_when((dist >= 0 & dist <= x) ~ "near",
            (dist > x & dist <= (2 * x)) ~ "far",
            T ~ NA_character_)
}

# Load data --------------------------------------------------------------------
length <- read_rds("wcpfc_length_data.rds")
catch_purse_seine <- read_rds("allrfmo_month_1deg_purseseine.rds")
catch_longline <- read_rds("allrfmo_month_5deg_longline_flag.rds")



data <- readRDS("rfmo_all_annual_gear_flag.rds") ### Data from JC's paper

effort <- data %>%
  mutate(id = paste(lat, lon, sep = "_")) %>%
  select(id, year, gear, grid, lat, lon, effort_measure, effort, contains("_mt"), contains("cpue_"))


#install.packages("sf")
library(sf)
lmpas <- st_read("clean_lmpas.gpkg") ### Data from JC's paper; this one is necessary for creating a spatial grid


## PROCESSING ##################################################################

# Find cells covered by MPAs ---------------------------------------------

#install.packages("terra")
library(terra)
# First, build some rasters
cells_1x1_within <-
  rast(nrows = 180, ncols = 360,
       xmin = -180, xmax = 180,
       ymin = -90, ymax = 90,
       nlyrs = 1, crs = "EPSG: 4326",
       resolution = 1, val = 1) %>%
  # Identify which cells are within an MPA polygon
  terra::extract(lmpas,
          xy = T,
          exact = T)  %>% # The `exact = T` argument calculates the percent cover
  mutate(grid = "1x1") %>%
  select(grid, lon = x, lat = y, fraction)

dim(cells_1x1_within) # There are 914 (781 without Johsnton) cells on the 1X1 grid that fall
# within an MPA. Note that not all these cells may have data reported by
# an RFMO and that not all are FULLY within an MPA... we'll get there

cells_5x5_within <-
  rast(nrows = 180, ncols = 360,
       xmin = -180, xmax = 180,
       ymin = -90, ymax = 90,
       nlyrs = 1, crs = "EPSG: 4326",
       resolution = 5, val = 1) %>%
  # Identify which cells are within an MPA polygon
  terra::extract(lmpas,
          xy = T,
          exact = T) %>%
  mutate(grid = "5x5") %>%
  select(grid, lon = x, lat = y, fraction)

dim(cells_5x5_within) # There are 97 (81 without Johnston) cells within an MPA using the 5x5 grid


cells_within <- bind_rows(cells_1x1_within,
                          cells_5x5_within) %>%
  filter(fraction >= 1) %>%
  select(-fraction)

# Build spatial grid -----------------------------------------------------------
# There are a few steps here:
# - First, build a grid of unique lat-lon combinations where RFMOs actually report
# some data
# - Then, remove cells that we've identified as being FULLY covered by an MPA
# - We then calculate the distance of each point to the nearest MP

# Create a single feature to keep things tidy
lmpas_sfc <- lmpas %>%
  st_union()

#install.packages("units")
library(units)

# length dataframe does not have a grid column, but you could easily add that field and make it 1x1 for PS and 5x5 for LL
length_onlyPSLL <- length %>%
  filter(gear %in% c("longline", "purse_seine")) %>%
  mutate(grid = case_when(gear == "longline" ~ "5x5",
                          gear == "purse_seine" ~ "1x1",
                          TRUE ~ NA_character_))

length_onlyPSLL %>%
  filter(is.na(lon) | is.na(lat))

rfmo_spat_grid_length <- length_onlyPSLL %>%
  select(grid, lat, lon) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lon), !is.na(lat)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  ### remove cells that fall fully within MPAs
  anti_join(cells_within, by = c("grid", "lat", "lon")) %>%
  ### convert to spatial object
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>% ### FLAG: try a more pacific-centered projection to see if it changes anything?
  #calculate distance to the nearest MPA
  mutate(dist = st_distance(., lmpas_sfc),
         dist = units::set_units(x = dist, value = "nautical_miles"), ### distances are now in nm
         dist = as.numeric(dist)) %>%
  ### keep only grid cells within 300 nautical miles of an MPA (note this is less than 600 that JC used but less clunky data is more gooder)
  filter(dist <= 300) %>%
  
  ### Build a series of dummies
  mutate(treatment_100 = assign_near_far(dist = dist, x = 100),
         treatment_200 = assign_near_far(dist = dist, x = 200),
         treatment_300 = assign_near_far(dist = dist, x = 300),
         near_100 = case_when(treatment_100 == "near" ~ 1,
                              treatment_100 == "far" ~ 0,
                              T ~ NA),
         near_200 = case_when(treatment_200 == "near" ~ 1,
                              treatment_200 == "far" ~ 0,
                              T ~ NA),
         near_300 = case_when(treatment_300 == "near" ~ 1,
                              treatment_300 == "far" ~ 0,
                              T ~ NA)) %>%
  # We now add information on which one is the nearest MPA
  st_join(lmpas, st_nearest_feature)

# Now convert it into a data frame ###FLAG: come back here to use code to make id field for data dataframe, so you can merge with your length data and plot alongside
rfmo_grid_length <- rfmo_spat_grid_length %>%
  bind_cols(st_coordinates(.)) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  rename(lon = X, lat = Y) %>%
  group_by(lat, lon) %>%
  mutate(id = cur_group_id()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(id, grid, lat, lon, wdpaid, name, dist, contains("treatment"), contains("near_"), ocean, year_enforced, month_enforced)




##````````` old 
# Make grid with distances and donuts ------------------------------------------
rfmo_spat_grid <- data %>%
  # Build distinct lat, lon pairs by grid type
  select(grid, lat, lon) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  # Remove cells identified as fully within an MPA
  anti_join(cells_within, by = c("grid", "lat", "lon")) %>% # This removes 110 grid cells that fall within an MPA and that have data
  # Convert into a spatial object
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  # Calculate distance to nearest MPA
  mutate(dist = st_distance(., lmpas_sfc),
         dist = units::set_units(x = dist, value = "nautical_miles"), # From now on, distances are in nautical mules
         dist = as.numeric(dist)) %>%
  # We'll keep only grid cells within 600 nautical miles of an MPA
  filter(dist <= 600) %>%
  # Build a series of dummies
  mutate(treatment_100 = assign_near_far(dist = dist, x = 100),
         treatment_200 = assign_near_far(dist = dist, x = 200),
         treatment_300 = assign_near_far(dist = dist, x = 300),
         near_100 = case_when(treatment_100 == "near" ~ 1,
                              treatment_100 == "far" ~ 0,
                              T ~ NA),
         near_200 = case_when(treatment_200 == "near" ~ 1,
                              treatment_200 == "far" ~ 0,
                              T ~ NA),
         near_300 = case_when(treatment_300 == "near" ~ 1,
                              treatment_300 == "far" ~ 0,
                              T ~ NA)) %>%
  # We now add information on which one is the nearest MPA
  st_join(lmpas, st_nearest_feature)

# Now convert it into a data frame
rfmo_grid <- rfmo_spat_grid %>%
  bind_cols(st_coordinates(.)) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  rename(lon = X, lat = Y) %>%
  group_by(lat, lon) %>%
  mutate(id = cur_group_id()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(id, grid, lat, lon, wdpaid, name, dist, contains("treatment"), contains("near_"), ocean, year_enforced, month_enforced)


## EXPORT ######################################################################
# saveRDS(object = rfmo_grid,
#         file = here("data", "processed", "distance_grid.rds"))
```


###Make panel
```{r}
# rfmo_grid_length is your spatial file, equivalent to distance_grid.rds
library(ggridges)
# Load data --------------------------------------------------------------------
distance_grid <- rfmo_grid_length
rfmo_data <- length_onlyPSLL

## PROCESSING ##################################################################

# X ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
combined <- rfmo_data %>%
  left_join(distance_grid, by = c("grid", "lon", "lat")) %>%
  mutate(id = paste(lat, lon, sep = "_"),
         event = year - year_enforced,
         post = 1 * (event >= 0))

combined <- combined %>%
  left_join(effort, by = c("year", "grid", "lon", "lat"))

##check_mt(combined, cutoff = 0) ##FLAG: check out what this does; I run into a vmem error so if it's not necessary keep commented out

#check_effort_gear(combined)

# X ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

#         file = here("data", "processed", "annual_panel.rds"))

#near_300; post

### Phoenix Islands Protected Area
```{r}
### ----- PIPA Longline bigeye pre/post protections ###FLAG: make sure the re-opening is captured properly
PIPA_LL_bet_length <- combined %>%
  filter(name == "Phoenix Islands Protected Area",
         post %in% c(0, 1),
         species == "BET", ### Keep bigeye tuna only
         gear == "longline") %>% ### Focus on longline
  mutate(yq = paste(year, quarter)) %>%
  select(yq, species, length_cm, post)

### Plot 
ggplot(data = PIPA_LL_bet_length,
       mapping = aes(x = length_cm,
                     y = factor(post))) +
  geom_density_ridges(vline_colour = "black",
                      vline_width = 1,
                      quantile_lines = T,
                      quantiles = 2) +
  labs(title = "Phoenix Islands bigeye longline average length")

### Quarterly median lengths
ggplot(data = PIPA_LL_bet_length,
       mapping = aes(x = length_cm,
                     y = factor(yq))) +
  geom_density_ridges(vline_colour = "black",
                      vline_width = 1,
                      quantile_lines = T,
                      quantiles = 2)

### Prepping data for line graph of yearly averages
PIPA_LL_bet <- combined %>%
  filter(name == "Phoenix Islands Protected Area",
         species == "BET",
         gear == "longline",
         !is.na(year))

### Average length by year
PIPA_LL_bet_length_line <- PIPA_LL_bet %>%
  filter(!is.na(length_cm)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(mean_length = mean(length_cm),
            n_length = n(),
            .groups = "drop")

### Use the shared IDs to select the corresponding effort records
PIPA_LL_bet_ids <- PIPA_LL_bet %>%
  filter(!is.na(id)) %>%
  distinct(id, year, gear)

### Average CPUE by year
PIPA_LL_bet_CPUE_year <- effort %>%
  semi_join(PIPA_LL_bet_ids, by = c("id", "year", "gear")) %>%
  filter(gear == "longline",
         !is.na(year),
         !is.na(cpue_bet)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(total_catch = sum(bet_mt, na.rm = TRUE),
            total_effort = sum(effort, na.rm = TRUE),
            cpue = total_catch / total_effort,
            .groups = "drop")

### Rescale CPUE to the length axis; the secondary axis reverses this scaling
PIPA_LL_bet_scale_factor <- max(PIPA_LL_bet_length_line$mean_length, na.rm = TRUE) /
  max(PIPA_LL_bet_CPUE_year$cpue, na.rm = TRUE)

### Length plot w/ effort
ggplot() +
  ### Length plot
  geom_line(data = PIPA_LL_bet_length_line,
            aes(x = year, y = mean_length, group = 1),
            color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = PIPA_LL_bet_length_line,
             aes(x = year, y = mean_length),
             color = "black",
             size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(data = PIPA_LL_bet_length_line,
              aes(x = year, y = mean_length, group = 1),
              method = "lm",
              se = FALSE,
              color = "black",
              linetype = "dashed") +
  ### CPUE plot (rescaled onto the length axis)
  geom_line(data = PIPA_LL_bet_CPUE_year,
            aes(x = year, y = cpue * PIPA_LL_bet_scale_factor, group = 1), color = "grey") +
  geom_point(data = PIPA_LL_bet_CPUE_year,
             aes(x = year, y = cpue * PIPA_LL_bet_scale_factor), color = "grey", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(data = PIPA_LL_bet_CPUE_year,
              aes(x = year, y = cpue * PIPA_LL_bet_scale_factor, group = 1),
              method = "lm",
              se = FALSE,
              color = "grey",
              linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Average length (cm)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / PIPA_LL_bet_scale_factor, name = paste("Average", "BET", "CPUE"))) +
  labs(x = "Sampling year",
       title = "Phoenix Islands BET longline average length and CPUE") +
  theme_classic()

         !is.na(year),

  geom_point(data = PIPA_PS_yft_length_line,

             color = "black",

  geom_smooth(data = PIPA_PS_yft_length_line,
              aes(x = year, y = mean_length, group = 1),
              method = "lm",
              se = FALSE,
              color = "black",
              linetype = "dashed") +
  ### CPUE plot (rescaled onto the length axis)
  geom_line(data = PIPA_PS_yft_CPUE_year,

  geom_point(data = PIPA_PS_yft_CPUE_year,

  geom_smooth(data = PIPA_PS_yft_CPUE_year,
              aes(x = year, y = cpue * PIPA_PS_yft_scale_factor, group = 1),

              se = FALSE,

  mutate(yq = paste(year, quarter)) %>%

### Plot

  labs(title = "PRI (Wake) skipjack longline average length")

### Quarterly median lengths
ggplot(data = Wake_LL_skj_length,
       mapping = aes(x = length_cm,
                     y = factor(yq))) +

                      vline_width = 1,
                      quantile_lines = T,
                      quantiles = 2)

### Prepping data for line graph of yearly averages
Wake_LL_skj <- combined %>%
  filter(name == "PRI (Wake)",
         species == "SKJ",
         gear == "longline",
         !is.na(year))

### Average length by year
Wake_LL_skj_length_line <- Wake_LL_skj %>%
  filter(!is.na(length_cm)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(mean_length = mean(length_cm),
            n_length = n(),
            .groups = "drop")

### Use the shared IDs to select the corresponding effort records
Wake_LL_skj_ids <- Wake_LL_skj %>%
  filter(!is.na(id)) %>%
  distinct(id, year, gear)

### Average CPUE by year
Wake_LL_skj_CPUE_year <- effort %>%
  semi_join(Wake_LL_skj_ids, by = c("id", "year", "gear")) %>%
  filter(gear == "longline",
         !is.na(year),
         !is.na(cpue_skj)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(total_catch = sum(skj_mt, na.rm = TRUE),
            total_effort = sum(effort, na.rm = TRUE),
            cpue = total_catch / total_effort,
            .groups = "drop")

### Rescale CPUE to the length axis; the secondary axis reverses this scaling
Wake_LL_skj_scale_factor <- max(Wake_LL_skj_length_line$mean_length, na.rm = TRUE) /
  max(Wake_LL_skj_CPUE_year$cpue, na.rm = TRUE)

### Length plot w/ effort
ggplot() +
  ### Length plot
  geom_line(data = Wake_LL_skj_length_line,
            aes(x = year, y = mean_length, group = 1),
            color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = Wake_LL_skj_length_line,
             aes(x = year, y = mean_length),
             color = "black",
             size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(data = Wake_LL_skj_length_line,
              aes(x = year, y = mean_length, group = 1),
              method = "lm",
              se = FALSE,
              color = "black",
              linetype = "dashed") +
  ### CPUE plot (rescaled onto the length axis)
  # geom_line(data = Wake_LL_skj_CPUE_year,
  #           aes(x = year, y = cpue * Wake_LL_skj_scale_factor, group = 1), color = "grey") +
  # geom_point(data = Wake_LL_skj_CPUE_year,
  #            aes(x = year, y = cpue * Wake_LL_skj_scale_factor), color = "grey", size = 3) +
  # geom_smooth(data = Wake_LL_skj_CPUE_year,
  #             aes(x = year, y = cpue * Wake_LL_skj_scale_factor, group = 1),
  #             method = "lm",
  #             se = FALSE,
  #             color = "grey",
  #             linetype = "dashed") +
  # scale_y_continuous(name = "Average length (cm)",
  #   sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / Wake_LL_skj_scale_factor, name = paste("Average", "SKJ", "CPUE"))) +
  labs(x = "Sampling year",
       title = "PRI (Wake) SKJ longline average length and CPUE") +
  theme_classic()

  filter(name == "Pitcairn Islands Marine Reserve",
         species == "BET",
         gear == "purse_seine",
         !is.na(year),
         !is.na(length_cm)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(mean_length = mean(length_cm),
            n = n(),
            .groups = "drop")

### Plot
ggplot(PIMR_PS_bet_length_line, aes(x = year, y = mean_length)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(color = "black"), size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(group = 1),
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("0" = "steelblue", "1" = "firebrick"),
    labels = c("0" = "Before protection", "1" = "After protection")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Sampling year",
    y = "Average length (cm)",
    color = NULL,
    title = "PIMR bigeye purse seine average length"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

  geom_point(aes(color = "black"), size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(group = 1),
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("0" = "steelblue", "1" = "firebrick"),
    labels = c("0" = "Before protection", "1" = "After protection")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Sampling year",
    y = "Average length (cm)",
    color = NULL,
    title = "NDMP bigeye longline average length"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
